financial_checks.claim: $1,250 a month (20% of $75,000) at 10% for 25 years about $1.54 million; at 7% about $979,000; principal $375,000
financial_checks.result: Effective-annual-rate monthly deposits: $1,541,656 (10%) and $978,802 (7%) match the video. Nominal monthly: $1,658,542 and $1,012,590. Annual contributions at 10%: $1,475,206, matching "$1.47 million". Conventions are mixed and unstated.

financial_checks.claim: Mia: $21,000 a year at 10% for 31 years from 34 to 65 is about $4.3 million, "more than Nick"
financial_checks.result: $3.99M (effective rate) to $4.39M (nominal monthly) at 10%; $2.21M-$2.31M at 7%. Nick's $750,000 at 10% to 65 is $3.79M ($2.37M at 7%) before his future saving: the comparison is not shown and reverses at 7%.
$743,000 holds; $7,000 is under one month of gross pay ($8,750).

financial_checks.claim: 760 versus 620 credit score on a $300,000 mortgage: $156 a month; $56,103 extra interest over 30 years
financial_checks.result: $156 x 360 = $56,160; internally consistent. The "according to myFICO" attribution was not checked; $156 implies about a 6.5% versus 7.3% rate gap.

financial_checks.claim: Missing the full match costs $1,336 a year, about $58,000 over 20 years at 7%; $24 billion unclaimed; one in four workers
financial_checks.result: $57,997 (monthly) or $54,770 (annual). The $1,336, $24 billion and one-in-four figures were not located.

financial_checks.result: Internal inconsistency: 3-6 months in the six-step list, 6-9 months in the path to 20%.

financial_checks.result: Not checked this session; the leak ranges and the trip premium are unsourced.

strengths: Compelling character paradox and a mechanism that is easy to remember.
The step ordering is explained causally.
Well-placed single subscribe ask and next-video pointer.
weaknesses: Compounding figures contradict each other ($1.54M versus $1.659M versus $1.47M).
The "Mia beats Nick" comparison ignores Nick's own growth.
Title overpromises a single "best advice" and loses the concrete part past character 55.
contradictions: $1.54 million versus "$979,000 to $1.47 million" for the same $1,250 a month.
3-6 months of emergency fund versus 6-9 months.
"Best financial advice you'll ever hear" versus a six-step list of standard advice.
Step six says to stop at about 15% (Fidelity) but the path says "the target is 20%".
Livermore made "approximately $100 million" in 1929 but "hundreds of millions" at the close.
improvement_opportunities: Retitle: "Do This The Day You Get Paid (The $743,000 Difference)" so the concrete action and number appear in the first 55 characters.
Show the compounding table once: $1,250 a month at 7% = $1.01M and at 10% = $1.66M, and use the same numbers in the closing.
Compare Mia at 65 with Nick at 65 (his $750,000 grown at the same rate) to make the end result honest.
Cut the repeated Livermore recap and one of the two system summaries.
Add the six steps to the thumbnail or on-screen as a numbered list.
